case_notes.note_type: Coaching / case management session – structured or in-depth meeting
case_notes.content:
### Session Summary

This session is a one-on-one meeting between a case manager/counselor and a client, **Nat Turner** (who references a background in Greenville and three years of sobriety), regarding his current housing situation, recovery stability, and paranoia/hypervigilance.

The client is currently residing at an **Oxford House** (sober living) in the Charleston area, which he views as the "headquarters" of his current recovery stability, though he is considering moving out due to discomfort and suspicion. Specifically, the client strongly believes that individuals are tampering with his property (loosening moped handlebars/brake cables), sneaking into his room to unlock his windows, and "jimmying" the exterior side door near his bedroom to gain entry. He had considered moving into a weekly hotel/motel for immediate independence, which the counselor strongly advised against due to high financial drain ($720–$790/week vs. ~$200/week at a halfway house), lack of accountability, and environmental triggers for relapse (using the "boiling frog" analogy).

The counselor validates the client's observations without feeding into his paranoid conclusions. Using self-disclosure about his own past experiences with manic/schizophrenic episodes and **confirmation bias**, the counselor helps the client reframe the "evidence"—pointing out that the client has no concrete history or enemies in Charleston who would target him, and that minor issues (like a misaligned exterior door from wear and tear) are likely being connected into a perceived plot due to overthinking and a "short-term reward focus". By the end of the session, the client agrees to hold off on moving to a hotel, acknowledges the need to consider alternative explanations, and agrees to keep his probation officer informed while they monitor the situation.

---

### Clinical Case Notes

**Client Name:** Nat Turner

**Setting:** Outpatient / Recovery Support & Case Management Session

**Sobriety Status:** 3 years clean (self-reported)

**Legal/Housing Status:** Currently on probation; residing in an Oxford House (sober living) in the Charleston area (relocated from Greenville).

#### Subjective (S)

* **Housing & Employment:** Client expressed dissatisfaction with his current Oxford House and explored alternative housing, including a cramped two-bed room and a weekly hotel ($720–$790/week). He noted he is making ~$16/hour ($450/week take-home) and previously transferred out of a Greenville facility so he could get his old job back rather than work a $10/hour job assigned through a prior program.


* **Paranoia / Persecutory Ideation:** Client reported strong beliefs that people at his current residence are targeting him. He cited a "stream of events" as proof: someone tampering with his moped's handlebars and brake cables, someone entering his room to unlock both of his windows, and someone "jimmying"/scraping the wood on the exterior side door near his bedroom so it won't latch properly.


* **Client Perspective:** Client stated, *"I'm not crazy... something ain't right,"* and insisted that even without knowing the perpetrator's motive, the physical signs prove malicious intent. He acknowledged working on his identified thinking patterns: *"justifying illegal behavior"* and *"short-term reward focus."*



#### Objective (O)

* Client presented as alert, engaged, and animated, becoming visibly frustrated and defensive when discussing perceived tampering at his house, though he remained receptive to rapport and humor with the counselor.


* Client showed photos on his phone of the door/screws to the counselor as evidence.


* Client demonstrated insight into the financial math of housing (recognizing $3,000/month for a hotel is unsustainable) and respected the counselor's feedback despite initial resistance.



#### Assessment (A)

* **Recovery & Housing Stability:** Client is at high risk of destabilizing his 3-year sobriety if he acts impulsively on his urge to leave sober living for an unstructured hotel environment. Moving to a hotel would introduce severe financial strain, environmental triggers (drug/prostitution activity), and a lack of accountability.


* **Cognitive Distortions / Hypervigilance:** Client is exhibiting significant **confirmation bias** and persecutory overthinking—linking unrelated maintenance issues (wear and tear on a shared exterior door) and past house conflicts into a cohesive narrative of being targeted. However, because he has no enemies or criminal history in Charleston, there is no logical motive for such targeting.


* **Progress:** Client responded well to grounded reality-testing and therapeutic self-disclosure. He successfully de-escalated, decided against the hotel move, and remained committed to following probation rules (not moving without prior PO approval).



#### Plan (P)

1. **Housing Retention:** Client will remain at his current Oxford House ("headquarters") and refrain from moving into a weekly hotel.


2. **Probation Compliance:** Client will maintain open communication with his probation officer (PO) before making any future address or housing changes.


3. **Cognitive Reframing & Monitoring:** Counselor and client will continue monitoring the living situation while practicing reality-testing to challenge confirmation bias, overthinking, and short-term reward impulses.


4. **Follow-Up:** Check in during next scheduled session regarding housing comfort, work schedule, and any further environmental concerns at the Oxford House.

case_notes.note_type: Coaching / case management session – structured or in-depth meeting
case_notes.content:
### Session Summary

A case manager conducted a structured one-on-one intake and goal-setting session with a client (Nat) enrolled in the **Turn 90** reentry program.

The session began with reviewing the client's personal history, identifying his core goals—securing a better job and personal growth—and briefly checking his background records in Greenville. The facilitator then guided the client through a cognitive-behavioral exercise using color-coded focus cards to identify his primary behavioral triggers (fear, pressure, and complacency following success), desired replacement behaviors, target skills, and concrete action steps. Finally, the two completed a readiness and barrier assessment covering documentation, health, finances, and transportation, followed by an in-depth discussion of the client's 30-year history with crack cocaine addiction, past relapses, and strategies for maintaining his current three-year sobriety.

---

### Case Notes

**Client Name:** Nat

**Program:** Turn 90

**Session Type:** Individual Case Management / Cognitive-Behavioral Planning & Intake Assessment

#### 1. Stated Goals

* Obtain better, stable employment.


* Achieve personal growth ("become a better person") and maintain lifelong recovery.



#### 2. Cognitive-Behavioral & Relapse Prevention Plan

The client selected two primary focus areas from the program's color-coded cards to structure his action plan:

* **Focus Area 1: Card B – Thinking Patterns**


* **Selected Sub-issues:** Justifying certain choices as necessary (**B3**) and focusing on immediate gratification ("what feels good now") over long-term impact (**B4**).


* **Triggers:** Feeling fearful about a situation and needing to make a major decision.


* **Replacement Behavior:** Pause and make better, well-thought-out decisions.


* **Target Skills:** Skills **7**, **15**, and **18**.


* **Action Items:**
1. Practice "stop and think" before acting.


2. List three possible consequences before acting on a risky choice.


3. Practice saying "no" to risky opportunities or high-pressure situations.






* **Focus Area 2: Card F – Substance Use**


* **Selected Sub-issue:** Using substances to deal with stress or emotions and to escape reality (**F2**).


* **Triggers:** Fear, difficulty coping with daily stressors, and **complacency/success** (feeling that achieving financial or material milestones means he has "made it" and can safely use again).


* **Replacement Behavior:** Stay clean regardless of fear or emotional discomfort.


* **Target Skills (Social Skills):** Skills **7**, **17**, and **18**.


* **Action Items:**
1. Identify one emotional trigger that increases the urge to use.


2. Reach out to one supportive person instead of isolating or using.


3. Track one situation where stress was successfully managed without using substances.







#### 3. High-Risk Environments & Boundaries

* Client confirmed he relocated from Greenville to avoid old neighborhood acquaintances and triggers.


* Identified four unavoidable public spaces where he might encounter old associates: **at a job, at a store, in traffic, and at a restaurant**. Client stated he avoids social hangouts and only visits places with a specific purpose.



#### 4. Substance Use & Recovery History

* **Primary Substance:** Crack cocaine (introduced at age 14; 30-year history of intermittent use, interspersed with periods of 2–5 years of sobriety).


* **Current Sobriety:** 3 years clean.


* **Relapse Patterns:** Past relapses were triggered by job loss, returning to selling drugs, entering unhealthy relationships, or experiencing career/material success (e.g., buying a car and regaining his license) which led to stopping NA meetings and believing he could use "successfully".


* **Protective Factors:** Active participation in NA meetings, Turn 90 classes, and strong motivation to avoid losing everything again.



#### 5. Barrier & Readiness Assessment

* **Identification & Vital Records:** Possesses Social Security card and birth certificate.


* **Legal / Driver's License:** Driver's license is currently suspended; staff member (Daisy) is assisting with fine reductions and license restoration.


* **Health & Vision:** No untreated illnesses or physical limitations affecting shift work. Needs an eye exam and glasses, though current vision does not prevent him from working.


* **Financial:** Does not have a traditional bank account (currently uses Cash App).


* **Work Attire:** Needs work clothes and work boots.


* **Transportation:** Currently relies on a moped.


* **Mental Health / Support:** Has a support plan in place to manage the transition back into the workforce.



#### 6. Next Steps & Action Plan

* **Case Manager:** Follow up with staff (Justin) regarding discrepancies in the client's automated computer assessment (specifically regarding financial stress and automatic reactions to unfair treatment, which the client stated did not accurately reflect him).


* **Program Support:** Coordinate assistance for work clothes/boots, vision care/glasses, and ongoing driver's license restoration with Daisy.


* **Client:** Complete written reflection worksheets based on today's selected cards, return to class following break, and attend next week's check-in.

case_notes.note_type: Documentation support – ID, housing forms, paperwork
case_notes.content:
Participant came in about housing. He is about to be put on contract at his Oxford House (Chippendale Rd, North Charleston 29420) because he hasn’t started working yet and still owes $370 on his deposit. The contract starts Monday, and he then has one more week to pay the full amount or he may be asked to leave. He asked whether Turn90 could cover the deposit. I explained that we can’t pay deposits directly. He also said the house is behind on its own bills and has raised everyone’s rent from $160 to $185 to catch up, which he doesn’t think should fall on him.

On the waitlist: he should be about second after the guys called in for orientation tomorrow, which likely means a 1–2 week wait. I said I’d ask TB and Justin whether there’s room for him to start Monday. That would put his first $450 stipend about two weeks out. I made clear I can’t guarantee it.

On employment: he has two job offers from box truck, where his record isn’t a barrier, but he needs his DL reinstated. He asked what happens if he's offered a job while he's on the waitlist. We talked through the choice. He can take a job now and stay in reentry navigation, or come through the 8-week program for a full-time placement. Since the program ends at 3pm, a second-shift or temp job alongside it is also possible. He said he’s committed to the program and sees the value in it. If he gets an offer, he’ll let us know, and I’ll check with Justin whether we could likely beat it.

On his license: he needs to pay $200 in reinstatement fees to the DMV and a $76 ticket in Greenwood ($276 total). He checked in with child support after release. They told him to call to set up a payment plan after the fees are paid. We submitted a Rainy Day Fund application during the meeting for $276: $200 to the DMV and $76 to the Greenwood ticket, with the ticket number included. I let him know decisions usually take 2–3 weeks, since funding opens at the start of the month and applications are reviewed toward the end.

On housing backup: if he’s asked to leave, we talked about transitional and sober living options. These included Lantern Residences (new North Charleston location, may have openings) and Calm Quarter. He does not want to live anywhere with people using drugs/drinking. Transportation shouldn’t be a barrier, because his father financed a moped for him and it’s working well. We also discussed asking the housing programs for a grace period, since he’ll have stipend income soon.

Other: his Android phone isn’t receiving texts from iPhones, so text outreach may not reach him and calls are safer. I offered food bank addresses and he said he already found one.
TB let me know that one guy he called in for orientation didn't get back to him, so I let Nat know that he can come in this week for orientation.

Grasshopper call recording failed.

Recently moved into a Charleston Oxford House on Ashley Phosphate from Greenville, SC. Has maintained sobriety for 3 years (3 years incarcerated, was released to a recovery program in September, and now intends to continue his sobriety post-release). Long past of crack cocaine use.

Main goal is to find employment so he can start paying his late rent. He has submitted over 20 job applications and has been going to staffing agencies but has been denied due to his record or offered jobs where he needs a license.

For transportation he uses his moped (has a moped license). Has all ID other than his DL. Owes $276 for reinstatement ($76 for a ticket, $200 for reinstatement). Made an appointment for tomorrow to submit an RDF referral.

He is also looking for help getting food. Does not qualify for food stamps because of past drug charges. I will send him food banks in his area.

Has child support arrears to pay off. Not currently paying more child support.

Overall is stable and committed to doing what he needs to do to join our program. Added him to waitlist and he wants reentry nav while he waits for a spot to open up.
